summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for recurrent hypoglycemia with associated confusion and memory loss, following a recent trip. She reported persistent symptoms despite recent medication changes, including discontinuation of octreotide and initiation of diazoxide. During the hospital stay, her glucose remained stable above 78 mg/dL, and a fasting study was not completed as her levels did not drop below the threshold. An endoscopy showed no acute ulcers but revealed abnormal mucosa in the esophagus and stomach. The metronidazole for bacterial overgrowth was discontinued, and her anti-nausea medication was changed to prochlorperazine. Tube feeds were cycled to nighttime only, and she was transitioned to a complex carbohydrate diet. She was discharged home with a revised diazoxide dosing schedule, nighttime tube feeding protocol, and follow-up planned in three weeks.
